notes: Kelteminar culture of the Kyzyl Kum and Karakum; the lead and infobox give 'c. 5500 BC - c. 3500 BC', 'a Neolithic archaeological culture of sedentary fishermen', 'discovered and first excavated in 1939'. Extent: 'in the territories of ancient Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan', 'the semi-desert and desert areas of the Karakum and Kyzyl Kum deserts', 'the deltas of the Amu Darya and Zeravshan rivers'; no area, no site list. Five admin-1 units (Karakalpakstan, Khorezm, Bukhoro, Tashauz, Qyzylorda) are drawn: Karakalpakstan and Khorezm and Tashauz for the Amu Darya delta, Bukhoro for the Zeravshan delta, Qyzylorda for the Kazakh part; the desert interior between them is not drawn (confidence 2, a placement). Relations: infobox 'Preceded by: Jeitun culture' (undated; the Jeitun dossier ends 4500 and keeps to the Kopet Dag); Mesolithic groups 'moved north into this area from the Hissar (6000-4000 BCE)'. After: 'replaced by the Tazabagyab culture' and the Suyargan and Boborykino cultures are listed as successors (no dates on the Kelteminar page); the Tazabagyab page dates the Tazabagyab 'ca. 1850-1500 BC' on the lower Amu Darya, so the land is nobody's from 3499 to 1850 on the pages opened. Some Russian scientists link the Kelteminar to the Pit-Comb Ware culture (not drawn). No area figure.
